overall: Graph WaveNet improves substantially over the submitted DCRNN runs, particularly short horizons. It has not established superiority over LightGBM or the team's GRU. Cross-model paired statistics here are explicitly post-hoc review analyses, not the original completed planned family.

matched_DCRNN_comparison.matched_scopes: GWN M4 vs DCRNN F (both external F634); secondary GWN M1 vs DCRNN DN (both domestic KR514 PM observations). Both seed11.
matched_DCRNN_comparison.2024_24h: CI includes zero; no significant improvement.
matched_DCRNN_comparison.domestic_comparison: GWN M1 has significantly lower RMSE than DCRNN DN at all four horizons in both splits, including Holm20 sensitivity. This also highlights the unusually weak/unstable DCRNN domestic fit, and should not be interpreted as proof of international information value.
matched_DCRNN_comparison.architecture_caveat: Inputs span comparable PM observations and fixed scoring rows, but graph type, temporal architecture, effective receptive field, optimization, regularization and head differ. Current GWN uses distance+adaptive, direct forecast, convolutional PM readout RF13h (48h loader), dropout0.3, Adam0.001 and weight decay0.0001. DCRNN used trajectory-directed seq2seq, 48h encoder, teacher forcing, dropout0, Adam0.01 and weight decay0. Thus the comparison is between actual submitted systems, not an isolated graph/architecture intervention.

local_LightGBM_reference.scope: F634 seed11, 2023 validation only; this is the local reference, not teammate B's independent latest run.
local_LightGBM_reference.conclusion: No significant paired difference at any horizon. GWN point estimates are slightly worse, especially 12h (~4.12%). Absence of significance is not evidence of equivalence.
local_LightGBM_reference.future: A raw-prediction 2024 LightGBM F634 same-grid comparison is not present among the verified sources.

published_team_sources.A: 2023 SARIMAX WNF 6.88/9.42/11.61/12.94. GWN M4 5.84/8.14/10.73/12.40 is numerically lower at all horizons. Raw A prediction keys absent, scopes differ, cannot claim paired significance.
published_team_sources.B_DOCX: 2023 LightGBM F600 three-seed ensemble 5.75/8.03/10.20/12.05. GWN M4 is numerically worse at all four horizons. Scope and seed aggregation differ, so this is descriptive.
published_team_sources.C_GRU_DOCX: 2023 GRU F600 three-seed ensemble 6.19/8.28/10.43/11.82. GWN M4 numerically improves 3/6h but worsens 12/24h. No general dominance.
published_team_sources.C_GCNGRU_DOCX: 2023 GCN-GRU F600 three-seed ensemble 6.76/8.98/10.99/12.28. GWN M4 numerically improves 3/6/12h but not 24h. Raw predictions absent and scope/seed mismatch.
published_team_sources.B_older_pasted_2024: B M3T 5.3100/7.1228/9.2843/10.8219; M4T 5.3435/7.1115/9.2748/10.9175. GWN M3T 5.7680/7.3079/9.3220/10.7383 and M4T 5.8688/7.5958/9.4445/10.7499 improve the old B figures only at 24h numerically. However B uses KR67 rather than KR514, fewer eligible rows (2840/2835/2828/2816 vs current 2874/2873/2871/2867), and old M3T has all-country trajectory mixing. No cross-model superiority should be asserted from these numbers.

interpretation: GWN domestic M1 is much more competitive than DCRNN DN. Hence DCRNN's large percentage gain from foreign inputs should not be treated as a universal need for foreign observations.
A model can improve the benchmark while adding foreign inputs does not significantly beat a strong domestic version. These are separate experimental questions.
GWN/DCRNN gains do not estimate pollution mass contributions, international cooperation savings, or source country attribution.
One seed does not establish reproducibility across initialization. Time-block confidence intervals quantify temporal sampling uncertainty conditional on the trained models, not seed uncertainty.

GWN's nominal 48-hour loader has eval-time PM convolutional receptive field13h under the paper profile; a larger receptive field is a separately controlled future architecture comparison, not a reason to silently relabel the completed experiment.
